full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This Civil Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 10.02.2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4219 of 2000 upholding the judgment and decree dated 28.02.2000 passed in Title Appeal No. 15 of 1997 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Gazipur which arose from the judgment and decree dated 31.10.1996 passed in Title Suit No. 19 of 1992 of the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur. 

 2. The respondent Nos. 1 to 25 herein, as plaintiffs, filed a partition suit in the 1st Court of Munsif, Gazipur in the year 1976 against the present defendant-petitioners and others and that suit, on transfer to the court of Additional Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur was renumbered as Title Suit No. 19 of 1992. The defendants in different sets contested in that partition suit. By the judgment and decree as aforementioned the trial court decreed that suit in preliminary form allotting a saham for 2.37 acres of land out of total 18.86 acres of divisible land to the plaintiffs. Being aggrieved by that judgment of the trial court different sets of contesting defendants filed four separate appeals being Title Appeal Nos. 15 Of 1997, 16 of 1997, 33 of 1997 and 35 of 1997 before the District Judge, Gazipur. The present leave petitioners filed Title Appeal No.  33 of 1997. However, all those four appeals were heard analogously by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and by a single judgment and order dated 28.02.2000 the appellate court allowed Title Appeal Nos. 15 of 1997, 16 of 1997 and 33 of 1997 by modifying the judgment and decree of the trial court reducing the share of the plaintiffs from 2.37 acres to 2.31 acres and giving saham of 8.00 acres of land to the defendant Nos. 128- 131 (the appellants of Title Appeal No. 16 of 1997). In that judgment the appellate court allowed the other defendant appellants of Title Appeal Nos.  33 of 1997 and 15 of 1997 to get separate saham for their respective purchased land from the appointed advocate commissioner on production of their purchase deeds to him. The appellate court, by that analogous judgment and order dismissed Title Appeal No. 55 of 1997. 

 9. It has already been stated above that the original partition suit was decreed on contest by the trial court by the judgment and order dated 31.10.1996 allotting a separate saham for 2.37 acres of land out of total 18.86 acres of divisible land to the plaintiffs. Being aggrieved by that judgment and decree of the trial court different sets of contesting defendants filed four separate appeals which were heard analogously by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and by a single judgment and order dated 28.02.2000 all these four appeals were disposed of The appellate court modified the judgment and decree of the trial court reducing the share of the plaintiffs from 2.37 acres to 2.31 acres of land and also giving saham of 8.00 acres of land to the defendant Nos. 128-131. Against that judgment and order of the appellate court below several civil revisions including Civil Revision Nos. 3762 of 2000, 3763 of 2000 and 3764 of 2000 were filed and the rules issued in all those civil revisions were ultimately discharged after hearing. The rules issued in Civil Revision Nos. 3762 of 2000, 3763 of 2000 and 3764 of 2000 were disposed of by single judgment dated 08.05.2005 against which the civil petition for leave to appeal Nos. 1461-1463 of 2005 were filed. The Appellate Division dismissed all those civil petitions for leave to appeal. So it appears that the judgment of the appellate court below was upheld upto the Appellate Division. So in the circumstances there is no necessity of entering into the merit of the case in this present civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 13. However, the present defendant-petitioners and other saham praying defendants may pray for saham to the trial court on production of their title deeds if, of course, in the meantime final decree of the partition suit has not been passed.
